subtopics.title: Iran-U.S. nuclear diplomacy: JCPOA to 2018
subtopics.summary: The Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (2015) set limits on Iran's nuclear programme in return for easing of international sanctions. The United States withdrew from the nuclear agreement in 2018. Iran then gradually scaled back its compliance with several JCPOA commitments.
facts: JCPOA was concluded in 2015 between Iran and the P5+1 countries.
Iran agreed to restrict uranium enrichment activities under the JCPOA.
Iran agreed to reduce its nuclear stockpiles under the JCPOA.
Iran agreed to permit enhanced international inspections under the JCPOA.
In return, international economic and financial sanctions on Iran were eased.
In 2018, the United States withdrew from the nuclear agreement.
Iran gradually scaled back compliance with several JCPOA commitments.
The scaled-back commitments related mainly to uranium enrichment and nuclear monitoring.

subtopics.title: IAEA: origins, objectives and leadership
subtopics.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency was founded in 1957 and is an intergovernmental organization. It grew out of the 1953 Atoms for Peace speech by US President Dwight D. Eisenhower. Its objectives are to promote peaceful use of nuclear energy and to inhibit its use for military purposes.
facts: IAEA was born out of US President Dwight D. Eisenhower's Atoms for Peace speech to the UNGA in 1953.
Objective: to promote peaceful use of nuclear energy.
Objective: to inhibit use of nuclear energy for any military purpose.
IAEA was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2005.
Head of the IAEA: Rafael Grossi.
Headquarters of the IAEA: Vienna, Austria.
